'''''Hitman 2'''''  is a 2018 [[Stealth game|stealth]] [[video game]] developed by [[IO Interactive]]. It is the seventh main installment in the ''[[Hitman (franchise)|Hitman]]'' video game series, the sequel to 2016's ''[[Hitman (2016 video game)|Hitman]]'' and the second game in the ''World of Assassination'' trilogy. The game continues the story arc started in ''Hitman'', following [[Genetic engineering|genetically engineered]] assassin [[Agent 47]] as he searches for the mysterious "Shadow Client" who is trying to destroy Providence, a secretive organization that controls global affairs. It also explores more of 47's mysterious background, which Providence offered to bring to light in exchange for 47's assistance. Like its predecessor, the game is structured around six large sandbox locations that players can freely explore to find opportunities to eliminate their targets. It also included two online multiplayer modes called Sniper Assassin and Ghost Mode, though the game's [[Server (computer)|server]]s for both modes have since been shut down; Sniper Assassin can still be played single-player.

The base game features six different locations: [[New Zealand]], [[Miami]], [[Colombia]], [[Mumbai]], [[Vermont]], and a fictional [[North Atlantic]] island called Sgàil. Two post-launch updates introduced locations set in [[New York City]] and the [[Maldives]]. Sales of 2016's ''Hitman'' fell short of expectations, prompting the series' publisher [[Square Enix]] to sell IO Interactive, which became an independent studio after a [[management buyout]]. With a limited cash flow, the studio laid off nearly half of its employees and had to reduce the scope of the sequel, whose development was about 25% completed. Because the framework had been created with the previous game, development of ''Hitman 2'' was faster than usual, taking about twenty-one months. The previous game's episodic model was abandoned and ''Hitman 2'' was released in full. IO Interactive supported the game with additional content after release, including two paid maps and free elusive targets and contracts.

''Hitman 2'' was released for [[PlayStation 4]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox One]] by [[Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment]]<!-- Do not change to Warner Bros. Games, the company published the game and lost rights years before the name change --> in November 2018, and for [[Google Stadia|Stadia]] by IO Interactive in September 2020. It received generally positive reviews, with most critics viewing it as an improvement over its predecessor and praising its varied locations, sandbox design, gameplay enhancements, humour and assassination opportunities. However, the story and the multiplayer modes was met with a mixed response. ''Hitman 2'' recuperated its development costs but its launch during a crowded release window negatively affected sales. ''[[Hitman 3]]'', the conclusion of the ''World of Assassination'' trilogy, was released in January 2021. In January 2023, ''Hitman 2'' was delisted from sales after IO Interactive rebranded ''Hitman 3'' as ''Hitman: World of Assassination'',{{efn|The ''World of Assassination'' branding was originally used for the Stadia release of ''Hitman 2'', and later ''Hitman 3''.}} with the contents of the previous two ''Hitman'' games becoming available to ''Hitman 3'' owners, free of charge.

== Gameplay ==
[[File:Hitman 2 gameplay screenshot.jpeg|thumb|left|In this gameplay screenshot, Agent 47 is disguising as a member of the Ark Society in the map of Isle of Sgàil.]]

Like the first game in the ''World of Assassination'' trilogy, ''Hitman 2'' is a [[stealth game]] that is played from a [[third-person perspective]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vg247.com/hitman-2-shows-grid-floor-security-cameras-looking|title=Hitman 2 shows you a grid on the floor where security cameras are looking|first=Kirk|last=McKeand|work=[[VG 247]]|date=3 July 2018|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=21 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921111751/https://www.vg247.com/hitman-2-shows-grid-floor-security-cameras-looking|url-status=live}}</ref> The player assumes control of [[Agent 47]], an assassin whose targets are scattered across the world. The game has eight missions that are set in [[Hawke's Bay]], New Zealand; [[Miami]], Florida; a village in [[Colombia]]; the slums of [[Mumbai]], India; a suburb of [[Vermont]] called Whittleton Creek; and a fictional North Atlantic island called Sgàil, set within the [[Northern Isles]] of [[Scotland]]. The game's [[downloadable content]] (DLC) includes new locations: a bank in [[New York City]] and a resort in the [[Maldives]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/every-map-from-hitman-1-2-and-3-ranked|title=Every level from Hitman 1, 2 and 3 ranked|first=Matthew|last=Castle|work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]|date=29 January 2021|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=3 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210903172239/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/every-map-from-hitman-1-2-and-3-ranked|url-status=live}}</ref> Players can download all of the chapters from ''Hitman'' if the player owns it or has bought the content as DLC, which incorporates the gameplay changes added to ''Hitman 2'' and allows ''Hitman'' to be played within ''Hitman 2''{{'}}s improved [[Game engine|engine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman-2/hitman-2-dlc|title=All 6 Hitman levels will be remastered as Hitman 2 DLC|first=Ali|last=Jones|work=[[PCGamesN]]|date=20 August 2018|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=10 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190910074940/https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman-2/hitman-2-dlc|url-status=live}}</ref> Each of the game's locations is a sandbox-type environment players can explore. Players must understand the layout of the maps to identify infiltration opportunities.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/11/16/18097468/hitman-2-silent-assassin-mastery-discovery|title=The two ways we play Hitman|first=Ryan|last=Gilliam|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=16 November 2018|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=10 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110002627/https://www.polygon.com/2018/11/16/18097468/hitman-2-silent-assassin-mastery-discovery|url-status=live}}</ref>

Gameplay structure and design are largely similar to those of ''Hitman'' (2016). ===Gameplay modes===
In addition to the single-player campaign, the game features several gameplay modes. Escalations are missions that include multiple stages. After completing each stage, the player will unlock the next stage which will increase the difficulty by adding additional targets or requirements (such as specific disguises or kill methods). Elusive targets are time-limited assassination missions that can only be attempted once. Contracts mode allows players to assign assassination targets, set requirements for their killings, and share their contracts with other players.<ref name="WB support"/>

''Hitman 2'' introduces two new game modes. In Sniper Assassin mode, players are tasked with eliminating targets from afar using a sniper rifle within 15 minutes. As in the main campaign, the NPC will react to the player's actions and each map has numerous assassination opportunities. This mode can be played solo or with other players, who will assume control of either Stone or Knight, characters who are equipped with concussive shockwave rounds and wall-piercing ammunition, respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/06/07/hitman-2-sniper-assassin-is-deep-fun-and-full-of-potential|title=Hitman 2 Sniper Assassin is Deep, Fun, and Full of Potential|first=Colin|last=MacGregor|work=[[IGN]]|date=7 June 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=24 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180924214010/http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/06/07/hitman-2-sniper-assassin-is-deep-fun-and-full-of-potential|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://kotaku.com/hitmans-sniper-assassin-mode-is-a-deadly-puzzlebox-1826682873|title=Hitman's Sniper Assassin Mode is a Deadly Puzzlebox|first=Heather|last=Alexandra|work=[[Kotaku]]|date=6 August 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=25 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125023933/https://kotaku.com/hitmans-sniper-assassin-mode-is-a-deadly-puzzlebox-1826682873|url-status=live}}</ref> Ghost Mode is a competitive, multiplayer mode in which two players must race against each other to eliminate assassination targets. Players start in the same location with no equipment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2018/gaming/news/hitman-2-ghost-mode-announced-1202978198/|title=Competitive 1V1 Multiplayer Ghost Mode Coming to 'Hitman 2'|first=Stefanie|last=Fogel|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=12 October 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=13 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200313184406/https://variety.com/2018/gaming/news/hitman-2-ghost-mode-announced-1202978198/|url-status=live}}</ref> The two players cannot directly interact with each other but can see the other player's avatar and will be notified when the other performs certain actions. They also share a target and ghost crates that contain disguises and weapons the players can use. The players who last discovers the crates may be left with inferior gadgets. If a player eliminates the target, the other player will have 20 seconds to eliminate their target in their world. Successful elimination of a target scores one point; the player who receives five points wins the game. Players lose one point if they kill a non-target character.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/if-youre-sick-to-death-of-battle-royale-rejoice-because-hitman-2s-ghost-mode-multiplayer-is-a-thrilling-1v1-assassination-race/|title=If you're sick to death of battle royale, rejoice because Hitman 2's Ghost Mode multiplayer is a thrilling 1v1 assassination race|first=Zoe|last=Delahunty-Light|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=12 October 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=18 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118190646/https://www.gamesradar.com/if-youre-sick-to-death-of-battle-royale-rejoice-because-hitman-2s-ghost-mode-multiplayer-is-a-thrilling-1v1-assassination-race/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Plot ==
Following the events of ''[[Hitman (2016 video game)|Hitman]]'', [[Agent 47]] embarks on a mission to find the mysterious "Shadow Client" for Providence, a secretive alliance of corporate executives, politicians, and industrialists collectively wielding political, military, and economic influence on the global scale. 47's employer, the International Contract Agency (ICA), has formed an uneasy alliance with Providence to stop the Shadow Client, whose actions are causing global panic, and 47 has agreed to help in return for Providence revealing his forgotten past. He begins by killing Alma Reynard, one of the Shadow Client's top lieutenants, in her home in [[New Zealand]], and Providence defectors Robert and Sierra Knox (father and daughter) at a racetrack in [[Miami]]. Meanwhile, the Providence leaders become angry at the killings of several CEOs and business tycoons associated with the group. Their immediate second-in-command, who first enlisted the ICA's services for Providence directly, formally identifies the Shadow Client as Lucas Grey, a former head of security for Providence who, from his hideout in [[Central Europe]], pursues his own plans with [[hacktivism|hacktivist]] Olivia Hall, intending to recruit 47 to help in his quest to destroy Providence.

In [[Colombia]], 47 assassinates Rico Delgado, Jorge Franco, and Andrea Martínez, leaders of a [[drug cartel]] who have been using their smuggling network and business connections to aid Grey and his militia. 47's handler Diana Burnwood reports the mission's success to Providence while visiting her family's graves in [[Surrey]], England. Flashbacks reveal she watched as her parents were killed by a [[car bomb]]. Grey and his team blow up the headquarters of Ether Biotech Corporation in [[Johannesburg]], steal an unidentified item, and take its CEO hostage in order to publicly reveal Providence's existence. In [[Mumbai]], 47 dismantles the militia's eastern cell by identifying and eliminating Grey's top lieutenant Wazir 'The Maelstrom' Kale and two of his associates, Vanya Shah and Dawood Rangan, who were responsible for the death of another Providence CEO.

47 follows Grey's trail to [[Romania]] and finds him at the asylum where he was created by Dr. Ort-Meyer.{{efn|As depicted in ''[[Hitman: Codename 47]]'' (2000)}} Grey reveals that he is also a genetically engineered [[Human cloning|clone]] created by Ort-Meyer, formerly known as Subject 6, and reminds 47 of their past friendship and vow to take revenge on those responsible for turning them into assassins. Grey reveals Ort-Meyer was a member of Providence, which he says is controlled by three executive members known as the "Partners" and their second-in-command, known as the "Constant". After Grey's and 47's plan to kill the Partners failed, the former managed to escape, but 47 was captured and had his memories erased. Grey aims to capture the Constant, who is the only person who knows the identities of the Partners. His only lead, however, is 47's knowledge of the identity of the first Constant from a visit to Ort-Meyer decades earlier. Grey reveals the item he stole in Johannesburg is an antidote that may counteract 47's memory loss. Diana is initially reluctant to work with Grey, arguing the ICA does not take sides, but eventually abides by 47's wishes to help Grey.

After taking the antidote, 47 recalls that the first Constant was a [[KGB]] spymaster known as Janus.  To avoid detection by the ICA and Providence, Diana files a false report implicating Janus as the Shadow Client while claiming Grey is a subordinate, giving 47 a pretext to assassinate Janus, who is living in [[Vermont]] after retiring. During the mission to assassinate Janus as well as the head of his security detail, Nolan Cassidy (so as to avoid Cassidy contradicting the report), 47 finds evidence that he was planning to meet the current Constant at a gala held by the "Ark Society", a plutocratic survivalist group founded by Janus during his tenure as Constant. The Partners, believing the report, coerce a resentful Constant into injecting himself with a chip that will release lethal poison into his body if he is compromised. After Hall locates the gala on a remote North Atlantic island, 47 travels there to capture the Constant and kill Zoe and Sophia Washington, the Ark Society's newly appointed chairwomen, who each hold a trigger for the chip. After neutralizing their triggers, the team is able to abduct the Constant.

After the mission, the Constant is taken to a ship to have the poison chip surgically removed and be interrogated about the Partners' identities. He reveals the Partners are representatives of Providence's founding families—the Ingram, Carlisle, and Stuyvesant families—and 47 and Grey leave to find them. The Constant taunts Diana, saying she does not know everything about 47. A final flashback depicts a young 47, under Providence's control, killing Diana's parents.

=== Downloadable content ===
As 47 and Grey begin their search for the Partners, Diana tells them Hall found recent obituaries for all three Partners, leaving the group to conclude the Partners faked their deaths and were planning to assume new identities. The Constant, seemingly unaware of this contingency plan, tells 47 and Grey to follow their bank accounts, which lead them to a [[New York City]] bank branch. 47 infiltrates the bank to retrieve data files, as well as kill its director and Providence operative Athena Savalas to prevent the Partners from discovering the data breach.

With the data acquired from the bank, Hall discovers the Partners paid large fees to Haven, a [[Maldives]]-based corporation that secretly creates new identities for wealthy criminals. To allow Hall to breach Haven's servers, 47 poses as a client to infiltrate the corporation's island resort and eliminate Haven's co-owners Ljudmila Vetrova, Steven Bradley, and Tyson Williams, to prevent them from resetting access to the servers at 10-hour intervals. Hall gains access to Haven's files on the Partners, and discovers that the controlling shares that comprise the backbone of Providence have not been allocated to the Partners' new identities, but rather to the Constant under his real name, Arthur Edwards. Diana rushes to check on Edwards but finds he has escaped. Hall obtains the locations of the Partners and informs 47 and Grey, who prepare to hunt them down, leading into the events of ''[[Hitman 3]]''.

== Development and release ==

=== Restructuring at IO Interactive ===
''Hitman 2'' was developed by Danish video game studio [[IO Interactive]]. The game's predecessor, which had an episodic release, received critical acclaim but missed the sales expectations of franchise and studio owner [[Square Enix]]. The team began developing a sequel that would incorporate online modes and more gameplay features while experimenting with new gameplay mechanisms. While preparing for game's production, in May 2017, Square Enix announced it had sold IO Interactive to concentrate resources on other studios.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/2017/5/11/15623158/io-interactive-square-enix-split-hitman |title=Square Enix drops Hitman developer IO Interactive |first=Samit |last=Sarkar |date=11 May 2017 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |access-date=10 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180831213743/https://www.polygon.com/2017/5/11/15623158/io-interactive-square-enix-split-hitman |archive-date=31 August 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> While Square Enix negotiated with potential buyers of the studio, IO Interactive became independent following a [[management buyout]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2017-11-22-its-not-hitman-without-io-why-square-enix-set-the-franchise-free|title="It's not Hitman without IO": Why Square Enix set the franchise free|first=James|last=Batcheolar|work=[[Gameindustry.biz]]|date=22 November 2017|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143321/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2017-11-22-its-not-hitman-without-io-why-square-enix-set-the-franchise-free|url-status=live}}</ref> The management of the IO Interactive, which had about 200 employees, had to lay off 40% of the workforce due to limited cash flow. ''Hitman 2''{{'}}s development was about 25% completed.<ref name="noclip main interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_stW6JvB4SI|title=The Rise and Fall of Hitman|work=[[Noclip]]|date=29 July 2019|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=11 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211130535/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_stW6JvB4SI&feature=applinks|url-status=live}}</ref>

After the buyout, IO Interactive owned the [[intellectual property]] (IP) of ''Hitman'' and decided to make the first episode [[free-to-play]]. The number of players nearly tripled and a significant portion of them bought the full game, ensuring a steady revenue for the studio. Due to limited manpower, the team had to limit the scale of the sequel and many planned features were cut. Development of ''Hitman 2'' progressed quickly due to the foundation of ''Hitman'' (2016), which was originally designed as a platform known as ''World of Assassination'' to allow the developer to add content. The late success of ''Hitman'' helped IO Interactive show there was a demand for this type of game, and the studio secured additional funding for the game's production.<ref name="noclip main interview"/> [[Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment]] signed to publish the sequel after partnering with IO Interactive on the Definitive Edition of ''Hitman''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mcvuk.com/business-news/publishing/calling-the-shots-how-hitman-2-made-the-move-to-warner-bros/|title=Calling the shots: How Hitman 2 made the move to Warner Bros|first=Seth|last=Barton|work=[[MCVUK]]|date=13 November 2018|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=16 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116035024/https://www.mcvuk.com/business-news/publishing/calling-the-shots-how-hitman-2-made-the-move-to-warner-bros/|url-status=live}}</ref> The game was [[Gone gold|declared gold]] on 27 September 2018<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-2-has-gone-gold/|title=Hitman 2 has gone gold|first=Samuel|last=Roberts|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=27 September 2018|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=27 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127023359/https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-2-has-gone-gold/|url-status=live}}</ref> after two and a half years of production with a development cost of $40 million– a significant reduction in time and cost compared to its predecessor due to the shared engine and assets.<ref> {{cite podcast| url= https://gamemakersnotebook.libsyn.com/exploring-the-world-of-hitman-with-io-interactives-hakan-abrak| title= Exploring the World of Hitman with IO Interactive's Hakan Abrak| website= Interactive.org| publisher= Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences Foundation| host= Orth, Adam| date= 19 December 2024| time= 50:13| access-date=26 February 2025}}</ref>

=== Design and story ===
The studio initially planned to include five massive maps in the game but decided to include six maps, some of which are smaller in scale.<ref name="noclip main interview"/> As the game was no longer episodic in structure, the team wanted the maps in the game to be more "consistent" in quality.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/10/18/17995428/hitman-2-io-interactive-sven-liebold-interview-gigantic-levels-columbia-ghost-mode|title=How Hitman 2's developers turned its gigantic levels into ever-evolving playgrounds|first=Nick|last=Statt|work=[[The Verge]]|date=October 19, 2018|accessdate=July 1, 2023|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020030248/https://www.theverge.com/2018/10/18/17995428/hitman-2-io-interactive-sven-liebold-interview-gigantic-levels-columbia-ghost-mode|url-status=live}}</ref> The game's locations were chosen early in the game's development; each level was assigned to a "track team" that would be responsible for its [[Level (video games)|level design]], targets, and opportunities. As with the original ''Hitman'', there are two types of levels in this game; "fortresses"—areas the player must infiltrate—and "snailhouses", levels with a circular design in which players are encouraged to explore the peripheral areas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/how-the-creators-of-hitman-use-social-science-to-design-perfect-murder-playgrounds/|title=How the creators of Hitman use social science to design perfect murder playgrounds|first=Joseph|last=Knoop|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=21 March 2019|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=3 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403145855/https://www.pcgamer.com/how-the-creators-of-hitman-use-social-science-to-design-perfect-murder-playgrounds/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EjvrTa6IKW8&t=967s|title=How the Simulation of a Hitman Level Works|work=Noclip|date=31 July 2019|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=21 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921111719/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EjvrTa6IKW8&t=967s|url-status=live}}</ref> The team visited the Maldives and Mumbai to ensure the locations in the game were authentic. According to the team, they did not intend to create an accurate version of these locations but wanted to "evoke the smells, tastes, and sounds of these places".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/how-io-made-the-hitman-trilogy-its-stealth-masterpiece/|title=How IO made the Hitman trilogy, its stealth masterpiece|first=Andy|last=Kelly|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=28 January 2021|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=7 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210307130401/https://www.pcgamer.com/how-io-made-the-hitman-trilogy-its-stealth-masterpiece/|url-status=live}}</ref> One of the design principles was to ensure each map would have spaces players could familiarize themselves with while providing an element of surprise by showing operations that are typically conducted in secret. For instance, players can disguise themselves to enter areas of a bank that are off-limits to the public. IO experimented with the two established designs. For instance, player must identify an unknown civilian as the assassination target and eliminate them in a public area in Mumbai. Track teams needed to decide on the items featured in each level. Items and outfits generally are categorized as specific items used for mission stories, and items that were designed to fit each map's aesthetic.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sQ0LlNfr8ZI&t=1274s|title=Revealing the Tricks Behind Hitman's Level Design|work=[[Noclip]]|date=5 August 2019|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=21 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921111810/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sQ0LlNfr8ZI&t=1274s|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Hitman 2'' added regional accents to many of its maps, such as the Mumbai and Colombia levels.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hitman 2 PC review – an expansive, astonishing sandbox |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman-2-pc-review |access-date=2022-04-26 |website=PCGamesN |date=8 November 2018 |language=en-GB |archive-date=2 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002105809/https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman-2-pc-review |url-status=live }}</ref>
<!--
IO Interactive described Miami as the "biggest level we have ever done" during pre-release interviews stating there are "almost 2000 NPCs in the crowd".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hitman 2 developer interview: 'Miami is the biggest level we have ever done' |url=https://www.shacknews.com/article/107085/hitman-2-developer-interview-miami-is-the-biggest-level-we-have-ever-done |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=Shacknews |date=6 September 2018 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-06-21 |title=Hitman 2 interview: How you'll knock out targets in giant crowds |url=https://venturebeat.com/2018/06/21/hitman-2-interview-how-youll-knock-out-targets-in-giant-crowds/ |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=VentureBeat |language=en-US}}</ref> The idea of the mission was appealing to developers as games set at race events usually have the player driving in the race whereas this mission would let players explore everywhere else like the paddocks and stands. They went back and forth on whether by default Sierra Knox should win the race but ultimately decided to make her lose so that players can make the decision to set her up to win themselves, which adds to player agency and provides a sense of [[poetic justice]]. The race will end after around 20 minutes, after which Knox will start wandering around the [[Very important person|VIP]] areas on foot, opening up new assassination opportunities. However, instead of forcing players to wait around the developers implemented ways to let players end the race early, allowing them to control the schedule of the level. The map layout is split into two halves with the race track down the middle, and each half is designed around one of the two targets. As a result, the level designers spent a lot of time finding many ways to let players cross the track such as overpasses and underground passageways.<ref>{{Citation |title=Making Hitman 2's Best Level |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=56iiP2xQn74 |language=en |access-date=2022-06-06}}</ref>

The New York DLC bank level was originally designed with side character Fabian Mann as a target as well as Athena Savalas, however IO were not sure what to do with the vault in the level or what to put inside it. They eventually decided that Mann should no longer be a target and instead made getting into the vault an objective of the level. To avoid the situation seen in the "[[Sapienza (Hitman)|Sapienza]]" mission from ''Hitman'' where IO said players felt forced to go down to the lab to destroy the virus every time they played, IO chose to let players decide to either break into the vault or instead collect a series of data disks carried by various characters (including Mann and Savalas).<ref name=":0" /> 
-->

While ''Hitman'' served as an introductory chapter to the ''World of Assassination'' series, ''Hitman 2''{{'}}s story has a more prominent role and a more structured narrative.<ref name="noclip main interview"/> ''Hitman'' was described as a "white collar new money" crime thriller whereas ''Hitman 2'' focuses on eccentric characters and "old money", which were inspired by [[secret societies]]. Much of the storytelling occurs within a level and during gameplay, and [[cutscene]]s mainly serve to tie together story threads.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/11/7/18068608/hitman-2-preview-ps4-xbox-one-pc|title=How Hitman 2's changes are designed for its bigger, deeper levels|first=Samit|last=Sarker|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=7 November 2018|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=8 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108103801/https://www.polygon.com/2018/11/7/18068608/hitman-2-preview-ps4-xbox-one-pc|url-status=live}}</ref> The abandonment of the episodic release model allowed IO Interactive to present a more cohesive story because players often forgot about narrative elements while they were playing ''Hitman'' due to its sparse release schedule. Like the first game, Agent 47 is a blank-state character and the story is mostly driven by his handler Diana Burnwood and Lucas Grey, both of whom have their own emotions, motivations and goals. Their presence allows Agent 47 to gradually develop as a character and foster change.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cf3bdBw99_Y&t=25s|title=Redesigning Hitman's Agent 47|work=[[Noclip]]|date=7 August 2019|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=21 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921111727/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cf3bdBw99_Y&t=25s|url-status=live}}</ref> The main story was written to motivate players to eliminate the targets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-2-isnt-just-about-killing-get-ready-to-find-out-even-more-about-agent-47s-past/|title=Hitman 2 isn't just about killing: get ready to find out even more about Agent 47's past|first=Zoe|last=Delahunty-Light|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=8 October 2016|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=23 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023090932/https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-2-isnt-just-about-killing-get-ready-to-find-out-even-more-about-agent-47s-past/|url-status=live}}</ref> Mission stories in ''Hitman 2'' were designed to encourage players to try out new gameplay features, tools, and costumes, while providing additional story content.<ref name="still weird">{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/6/18/17475484/hitman-2-preview-hands-on-e3-2018|title=Hitman 2 is still as weird as ever|first=Chelsea|last=Stark|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=18 June 2016|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=9 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109025100/https://www.polygon.com/2018/6/18/17475484/hitman-2-preview-hands-on-e3-2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Developers were careful to ensure the game was hitting the right tone, recasting a more mature-sounding actor for Alma Reynard (the target from the opening New Zealand mission) and giving her a new outfit after the original take was "too young-sounding" in order to avoid the game becoming "too creepy or sexually predatory".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-23 |title=Deep Dive into HITMAN 3 - Game Informer |url=https://www.hitmanforum.com/t/deep-dive-into-hitman-3-game-informer/59 |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=Hitman Forum |language=en |archive-date=24 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201224211546/https://www.hitmanforum.com/t/deep-dive-into-hitman-3-game-informer/59 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The game includes extensive [[dark humour]]; early promotion of the game showed Agent 47 whacking NPCs with a fish.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vg247.com/hitman-3-will-mature-serious-darker-tone|title=Hitman 3 will be "more mature, serious, darker" and probably won't let you slap a man with a fish|first=Kirk|last=McKeand|work=[[VG247]]|date=25 June 2020|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=21 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921111740/https://www.vg247.com/hitman-3-will-mature-serious-darker-tone|url-status=live}}</ref> According to Markus Friedl, the game's executive producer, "this little bit of [[tongue-in-cheek]] humor [is] very much part of the ''Hitman'' DNA".<ref name="still weird"/> [[David Bateson]], who provides the voice of Agent 47, initially thought some of the dialogue was absurd but grew to appreciate it after understanding how mission stories work. According to Bateson, while Agent 47 is an expert at disguising himself, he is a terrible actor. He was instructed not to change his accent when disguised as other personalities and he delivered his lines in a "delightfully wooden way".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/david-bateson-on-20-years-of-playing-hitmans-agent-47-hes-my-best-friend/|title=David Bateson on 20 years of playing Hitman's Agent 47: 'He's my best friend!'|first=Andy|last=Kelly|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=26 February 2021|accessdate=20 September 2021|archive-date=2 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302200929/https://www.pcgamer.com/david-bateson-on-20-years-of-playing-hitmans-agent-47-hes-my-best-friend/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Release==
[[File:Sean Bean TIFF 2015.jpg|thumb|180px|right|[[Sean Bean]] portrayed the game's first Elusive Target, "The Undying"]]

Warner Bros. announced ''Hitman 2'' on 7 June 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/6/7/17438546/hitman-2-io-interactive-agent-47-announced-e3-2018-xbox-one-ps4-pc|title=Hitman 2 will introduce co-op assassinations this November|first=Chaim|last=Gartenberg|work=[[The Verge]]|date=7 June 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=14 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614005912/https://www.theverge.com/2018/6/7/17438546/hitman-2-io-interactive-agent-47-announced-e3-2018-xbox-one-ps4-pc|url-status=live}}</ref> The game did not follow its predecessor's episodic release model after the developers received negative feedback from players of the first game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2018-09-05-io-interactive-focusing-on-serving-players-not-games-as-a-service|title=IO Interactive focusing on serving players, not games-as-a-service|first=Rebekah|last=Valentine|work=[[Gameindustry.biz]]|date=5 September 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=20 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420020510/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2018-09-05-io-interactive-focusing-on-serving-players-not-games-as-a-service|url-status=live}}</ref> Players who pre-ordered the game gained immediate access to Sniper Assassin mode. In July 2018, IO Interactive announced a competition for Sniper Assassin players; the top-three players with the highest scores would have the opportunity to have their names and likeness incorporated into the game's post-release content.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/2018/07/26/hitman-2-competition-makes-you-a-target-for-agent-47|title=Hitman 2 Competition Makes You A Target For Agent 47|first=Imran|last=Khan|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=26 July 2018|access-date=21 September 2021|archive-date=26 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126034201/https://www.gameinformer.com/2018/07/26/hitman-2-competition-makes-you-a-target-for-agent-47|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Hitman 2'' was released worldwide for [[PlayStation 4]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox One]] on 13 November 2018,<ref>{{cite web|last=Sheridan|first=Connor|date=8 June 2018|title=Hitman 2 has a release date and a cool pre-order bonus: a co-op sniping game out now|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-2-has-a-release-date-and-a-cool-pre-order-bonus-a-co-op-sniping-game-out-now/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022123638/https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-2-has-a-release-date-and-a-cool-pre-order-bonus-a-co-op-sniping-game-out-now/|archive-date=22 October 2020|work=[[GamesRadar]]|accessdate=29 November 2021}}</ref> although those who pre-ordered the game's gold edition gained access to the game four days earlier.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-2-release-times/|title=Here are Hitman 2's release date timings|first=Fraser|last=Brown|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=8 November 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=30 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130054300/https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-2-release-times/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 1 September 2020, IO Interactive released ''Hitman 2'' for [[Google Stadia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gematsu.com/2020/07/hitman-and-hitman-2-coming-to-stadia-on-september-1-hitman-3-coming-in-january-2021|title=Hitman and Hitman 2 coming to Stadia on 1 September, Hitman 3 coming in January 2021|first=Sal|last=Romano|work=Gematsu|date=14 July 2021|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=27 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227211352/https://www.gematsu.com/2020/07/hitman-and-hitman-2-coming-to-stadia-on-september-1-hitman-3-coming-in-january-2021|url-status=live}}</ref> The first level was made free-to-play on 27 February 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-2s-first-mission-is-now-free-for-everyone/|title=Hitman 2's first mission is now free for everyone|first=Andy|last=Chalk|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=27 February 2019|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=15 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190615113045/https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-2s-first-mission-is-now-free-for-everyone/|url-status=live}}</ref>

IO Interactive extensively supported ''Hitman 2'' with DLC, and regularly added escalation targets, challenge packs and elusive targets into the game. [[Sean Bean]] portrayed the game's first elusive target Mark Faba in the Miami map. This mission, which is titled "The Undying", was released on 18 November 2018, a week after the game's release.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-11-21-you-can-now-hunt-down-sean-bean-as-hitman-2s-first-elusive-target-mission-gets-underway|title=You can now hunt down Sean Bean as Hitman 2's first Elusive Target|first=Matt|last=Wales|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=21 November 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=6 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206195450/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-11-21-you-can-now-hunt-down-sean-bean-as-hitman-2s-first-elusive-target-mission-gets-underway|url-status=live}}</ref> A temporary seasonal [[Sapporo Snow Festival|snow festival]] event set on the [[Hokkaido]] map from ''Hitman'' was added on 22 January 2019,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sarkar |first=Samit |date=2019-01-21 |title=Wintry Hitman 2 update lets Agent 47 throw snowballs in Japan |url=https://www.polygon.com/2019/1/21/18191775/hitman-2-update-patch-notes-snow-festival |access-date=2022-04-17 |website=Polygon |language=en-US |archive-date=17 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220417012649/https://www.polygon.com/2019/1/21/18191775/hitman-2-update-patch-notes-snow-festival |url-status=live }}</ref> later being permanently added in December that same year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-12-13 |title=HITMAN 2 - December Roadmap |url=https://www.ioi.dk/hitman-2-october-roadmap/ |access-date=2022-04-17 |website=IO Interactive |language=en-US |archive-date=27 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627195711/https://www.ioi.dk/hitman-2-october-roadmap/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> A unique Halloween themed escalation called "The Mills Reverie" was released in October 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-22 |title=Hitman 2: Halloween Event - How To Complete The Mills Reverie {{!}} Secret Rewards Guide |url=https://gameranx.com/features/id/185278/article/hitman-2-halloween-event-how-to-complete-the-mills-reverie-secret-rewards-guide/ |access-date=2022-04-17 |website=Gameranx |language=en-US |archive-date=7 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220907141510/https://gameranx.com/features/id/185278/article/hitman-2-halloween-event-how-to-complete-the-mills-reverie-secret-rewards-guide/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-02 |title=HITMAN 2 - October Roadmap |url=https://www.ioi.dk/hitman-2-october-roadmap/ |access-date=2022-04-17 |website=IO Interactive |language=en-US |archive-date=27 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627195711/https://www.ioi.dk/hitman-2-october-roadmap/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The game suffered an early [[Bug (computing)|bug]] that was referred to as the "homing briefcase", which was triggered when a briefcase was thrown at a target; the briefcase would spin and fly slowly towards the target, even if the target moved around the level. The homing behaviour is an intentional feature of all thrown melee items in ''Hitman'' but the speed was unusual.<ref name="pcgamer-homing">{{cite web | url = https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-2-homing-briefcase/ | title = I can't stop laughing at Hitman 2's homing briefcase | first = Tyler | last = Wilde | date = 13 November 2018 | access-date = 9 August 2019 | work = [[PC Gamer]] | archive-date = 9 August 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190809224156/https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-2-homing-briefcase/ | url-status = live }}</ref> IO patched the game and the developers acknowledged the bug, adding a special briefcase item, the Executive Briefcase MKII, that restored the slow-homing speed. The item was released on 8 August 2019 as part of the "Best Case Scenario" challenge pack.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.polygon.com/2019/8/3/20752919/hitman-2-august-2019-roadmap-pc-ps4-xbox-one | title = Hitman's heat-seeking briefcase is officially a weapon in the next update | first = Owen | last = Good | date = 3 August 2019 | access-date = 9 August 2019 | work = [[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] | archive-date = 8 August 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190808155920/https://www.polygon.com/2019/8/3/20752919/hitman-2-august-2019-roadmap-pc-ps4-xbox-one | url-status = live }}</ref>

Following the game's initial release, two paid expansions, each of which added new locations, missions, outfits, and weapons, were announced. The first expansion added a new main mission set in a bank in [[New York City]] as well as two single target "special assignment" missions set on variants of the Mumbai and Colombia maps on 25 June 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2019/6/24/18715926/hitman-2-expansion-the-bank-release-date-trailer-new-york-mastery|title=Hitman 2's first expansion takes Agent 47 to New Sniper Assassin map called Hantu Port set in [[Singapore]] was released as part of the first expansion on 26 March 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last=Tarason |first=Dominic |date=26 March 2019 |title=Hitman 2 goes sniping at Hantu Port in its first paid DLC level |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/ian-heads-to-singapore-in-the-first-paid-hitman-2-dlc |url-status=live |accessdate=21 September 2021}}</ref> The second expansion added another main mission set on Haven Island, an island in the Maldives, and two more special assignments set in Miami and Whittleton Creek on 24 September 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-09-19-hitman-2-gets-tropical-next-week-in-new-maldives-resort-dlc-haven-island|title=Hitman 2 gets tropical next week in new Maldives resort DLC, Haven Island|website=Eurogamer|last1=Wales|first1=Matt|date=17 September 2019|access-date=8 April 2020|archive-date=7 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191207061526/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-09-19-hitman-2-gets-tropical-next-week-in-new-maldives-resort-dlc-haven-island|url-status=live}}</ref> It also added another Sniper Assassin map set in a [[Siberia]]n prison on 30 July 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-07-29-hitman-2s-off-to-siberia-in-new-sniper-assassin-map|title=Hitman 2's off to Siberia this week in new Sniper Assassin map|first=Matt|last=Wales|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=29 July 2019|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=1 March ''Hitman 2'' received "generally favorable" reviews, according to [[review aggregator]] platform [[Metacritic]].{{r|MCPS4|MCONE|MCPC}} Reviewers agreed the game does not significantly deviate from its predecessor's formula but they enjoyed the general gameplay loop and its improvements.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vg247.com/hitman-2-review|title=Hitman 2 review: assassinating sequel delivers killer ideas in spades|first=Dave|last=Meikelhem|work=[[VG247]]|date=8 November 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=21 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921111721/https://www.vg247.com/hitman-2-review|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="GRRev"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/11/13/18089674/hitman-2-review-ps4-xbox-pc|title=Hitman 2 is the most refined and rewarding game in the series|first=Nick|last=Slatt|work=[[The Verge]]|date=13 November 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=16 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116085335/https://www.theverge.com/2018/11/13/18089674/hitman-2-review-ps4-xbox-pc|url-status=live}}</ref> Some game journalists said the episodic model of ''Hitman'' helped players thoroughly explore each level and were disappointed IO Interactive abandoned this release strategy for ''Hitman 2''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamerevolution.com/features/456349-why-hitman-2-should-be-episodic|title=Why Hitman 2 Should Be Episodic|first=Rose|last=Kelly|work=[[Game Revolution]]|date=14 November 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=3 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201203014758/https://www.gamerevolution.com/features/456349-why-hitman-2-should-be-episodic|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usgamer.net/articles/hitman-2-going-in-a-non-episodic-direction-is-a-huge-disappointment|title=Hitman 2 Going in a Non-Episodic Direction is a Huge Disappointment|first=Caty|last=McCarthy|work=[[USgamer]]|date=7 June 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=19 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210719113932/https://www.usgamer.net/articles/hitman-2-going-in-a-non-episodic-direction-is-a-huge-disappointment|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Hitman 2''{{'s}} design received critical praise. Phil Savage from ''[[PC Gamer]]'' strongly praised five of the game's six maps, and described them as "large" and "intricate". He added the quality of the maps is more consistent than those of the first game. He said, however, ''Hitman 2'' did not extensively experiment with the formula and that the game simply "riffs on familiar design principles".<ref name="PCGRev"/> Writing for ''[[GameSpot]]'', Edmon Tran described the maps as "overwhelming in the best way possible" and singled out Mumbai as one of the game's standout maps.<ref name="GSpotRev"/> Many reviewers praised the diversity of the maps, each of which is set in visually unique locations with their own characters and routes.<ref name="VBRev"/><ref name="GIRev"/> Caty McCarthy from ''[[USgamer]]'' praised IO for perfecting the formula established in its predecessor and said all levels reached the quality of [[Sapienza (Hitman)|Sapienza]], which is widely recognized as ''Hitman''{{'s}} best map.<ref name="USGRev"/> ''[[Destructoid]]''{{'}}s Chris Carter agreed, and said "''Hitman 2'' is a colossal collection of puzzles begging to be solved through multiple playthroughs".<ref name="DestructRev"/> The Legacy content received praise for introducing gameplay adjustments to older ''Hitman'' levels.<ref name="USGRev"/><ref name="GRRev"/>

The gameplay received generally positive reviews. Several reviewers said the game offers players too much guidance, making exploration and discovery of creative assassinations less organic.<ref name="GIRev"/><ref name="PCGRev"/> Savage liked the gameplay enhancements but said familiar problems of the franchise had not been solved.<ref name="PCGRev"/> Tran enjoyed the core gameplay loop of slowly discovering a location and its stories. While the gameplay is built on trial and error, he said the game becomes more exciting when the players' plan fails, forcing them to improvise.<ref name="GSpotRev"/> ''[[IGN]]''{{'}}s Ryan McCaffery praised the developers for allowing players to freely approach their objectives and liked the mission stories for presenting memorable and unique gameplay moments, and making successful assassinations a satisfying gameplay experience.<ref name="IGNRev"/> McCarthy praised the dialogue of the mission stories, describing it as "sharper and funnier", and adding the script "adds to the silly fun of the ''Hitman'' universe".<ref name="USGRev"/> Many reviewers agreed players can only understand the intricacies of the game's system and the availability of the options presented to them by replaying it.<ref name="IGNRev"/><ref name="EuroGRev"/><ref name="GRRev"/> Minor gameplay adjustments IO Interactive added to the game were also appreciated.<ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref name="IGNRev"/><ref name="GBRev"/>

Ghost mode had a divided reception; some reviewers said its design does not well complement the slow, methodical gameplay of the single-player campaign.<ref name="GBRev"/><ref name="IGNRev"/><ref name="GIRev"/> Some reviewers, however, said it is a fun, satisfying experience.<ref name="EuroGRev">{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-11-08-hitman-2-review-a-surgical-to-the-point-of-slender-sequel|title=Hitman 2 review - a surgical to the point of slender sequel|first=Edwin|last=Evans-Thirlwell|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=8 November 2018|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=1 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210901114107/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-11-08-hitman-2-review-a-surgical-to-the-point-of-slender-sequel|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="GRRev" /> Some reviewers expressed disappointment Sniper Assassin had only one map at launch.<ref name="GRRev"/><ref name="GIRev"/>

The game's story received mixed reviews. McCaffery was disappointed by the overarching story; he called it "absurdly dumb" and poorly presented, and said the game's attempt at exploring Agent 47's backstory is as bad as that of [[Hitman (2007 film)|the 2007 ''Hitman'' film]].<ref name="IGNRev"/> Brad Shoemaker, writing for ''[[Giant Bomb]]'', found the main story surprisingly engaging; he described it as a "taut international cat-and-mouse thriller", and appreciated the story for raising the stakes and resolving the mysteries of the first game. He agreed, however, the game does not have the production quality of ''Hitman'', which is evidenced by the lack of CGI cutscenes,<ref name="GBRev"/> instead opting for static images and voice-overs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kotaku.com/no-one-warned-me-about-hitman-2-s-cutscenes-1846655303|title=No One Warned Me About Hitman 2's Cutscenes|first=Ari|last=Notis|work=[[Kotaku]]|date=4 September 2021|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=11 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210811151610/https://kotaku.com/no-one-warned-me-about-hitman-2-s-cutscenes-1846655303|url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Game Informer]]'', Jeff Marchiafava said the [[storyboard]] sequences are "cheap and disappointing", especially since the first game has lavishly produced videos and in-engine graphics.<ref name="GIRev"/>

=== Sales ===
''Hitman 2'' debuted at tenth place in the UK's all-format sales charts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-11-19-spyro-sold-more-physical-copies-at-launch-than-fallout-76|title=Spyro sold more physical copies at launch than Fallout 76|first=Tom|last=Phillips|date=19 November 2018|website=[[Eurogamer]]|publisher=Gamer Network|access-date=19 November 2018|archive-date=19 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181119141527/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-11-19-spyro-sold-more-physical-copies-at-launch-than-fallout-76|url-status=live}}</ref> It was released in a competitive week that also saw the launches of ''[[Pokémon: Let's Go]]'', ''[[Spyro Reignited Trilogy]]'' and ''[[Fallout 76]]''.<ref name="gamesindustry">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2018-11-18-pok-mon-and-spyro-top-hyper-competitive-week-at-uk-games-retail|title=Pokémon and Spyro top hyper competitive week at UK games retail|first=Christopher|last=Dring|date=18 November 2018|work=[[GamesIndustry.biz]]|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=6 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206173420/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2018-11-18-pok-mon-and-spyro-top-hyper-competitive-week-at-uk-games-retail|url-status=live}}</ref> In Japan, the PlayStation 4 version sold 10,162 copies in its debut week, making it the week's fifth-best-selling retail game in the country.<ref>{{cite web |last=Romano |first=Sal |date=21 November 2018 |url=https://gematsu.com/2018/11/media-create-sales-11-12-18-11-18-18 |title=Media Create Sales: 11/12/18 – 11/18/18 |publisher=Gematsu |access-date=4 October 2019 |archive-date=16 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216120622/https://gematsu.com/2018/11/media-create-sales-11-12-18-11-18-18 |url-status=live }}</ref> IO Interactive CEO Hakan Abrak said releasing the game so close to other blockbuster titles such as ''[[Red Dead Redemption 2]]'' negatively impacted the game's sales.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2021-04-28-how-io-interactive-realised-its-complete-vision-of-hitman-through-self-publishing|title=How IO Interactive realised its full vision for Hitman's World of Assassination trilogy|first=Alan|last=Wen|work=[[Gameindustry.biz]]|date=28 April 2021|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=10 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210910233535/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2021-04-28-how-io-interactive-realised-its-complete-vision-of-hitman-through-self-publishing|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Hitman 2'', however, recouped its development cost more quickly than ''Hitman'' had.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/hitman-studio-io-came-close-to-accepting-really-attractive-acquisition-offers/|title=Hitman studio IO says it received 'really attractive' acquisition offers|first=Tom|last=Ivan|work=Video Games Chronicle|date=7 April 2021|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=7 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210707203607/https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/hitman-studio-io-came-close-to-accepting-really-attractive-acquisition-offers/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Accolades ===
''Hitman 2'' was nominated for Game of the Year during the 2018 [[Steam Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Steam Awards 2018 Winners |url=https://store.steampowered.com/SteamAwards/2018/ |access-date=2022-04-17 |website=store.steampowered.com |language=en |archive-date=18 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220418001726/https://store.steampowered.com/SteamAwards/2018/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was voted the best stealth game of the year at the 2018 Global Game Awards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Best Stealth Award Global Game Awards 2018 |url=https://www.game-debate.com/awards/2018/best-stealth |access-date=2022-04-18 |website=www.game-debate.com |language=en |archive-date=30 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211230010127/https://www.game-debate.com/awards/2018/best-stealth |url-status=live }}</ref> The game was also nominated for "Game, Franchise Adventure" and "Control Design, 3D" at the [[Video game award#NAVGTR Awards|NAVGTR Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 Awards {{!}} NAVGTR |url=https://navgtr.org/2018-awards/ |access-date=2022-04-18 |language=en-US |archive-date=14 March 2019 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190314083147/http://navgtr.org/archives/3601/ |url-status=live }}</ref> David Bateson was nominated for "Outstanding Video Game Character, Best Voiceover" for his performance as Agent 47 in ''Hitman 2'' at the 2019 Society of Voice Arts And Sciences Awards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 Nominees |url=https://www.sovas.org/2019-nominees/ |access-date=2022-04-18 |website=Sovas |language=en-US |archive-date=16 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216215756/https://www.sovas.org/2019-nominees/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Sequel ==
{{Main|Hitman 3}}
''Hitman 3'', the sequel to ''Hitman 2'' and the conclusion of the ''World of Assassination'' trilogy, was released in January 2021. It was published by IO Interactive.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vg247.com/io-interactive-will-self-publish-hitman-3|title=IO Interactive will self-publish Hitman 3|first=Stephanny|last=Nunneley|work=[[VG247]]|date=25 June 2020|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=21 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921111721/https://www.vg247.com/io-interactive-will-self-publish-hitman-3|url-status=live}}</ref> Because the sequel does not include any competitive online modes, IO Interactive shut down the ''Hitman 2'' servers on 31 August 2021. While Sniper Assassin can be played offline, Ghost Mode and the online aspect of Sniper Assassin became unplayable once the servers were taken offline.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/hitman-3-wont-have-ghost-mode-and-hitman-2-is-shutting-down-multiplayer-servers|title=Hitman 3 won't have Ghost Mode, and Hitman 2 is shutting down multiplayer servers|first=Alice|last=O'Connor|work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]|date=18 August 2020|accessdate=21 September 2021|archive-date=24 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210424005434/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/hitman-3-wont-have-ghost-mode-and-hitman-2-is-shutting-down-multiplayer-servers|url-status=live}}</ref> The Ambrose Island location added to ''Hitman 3'' for free on 26 July 2022 is set during the events of ''Hitman 2'', between the Whittleton Creek and Isle of Sgàil missions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-27 |title=Hitman 3 Just Got A Free New Level, Which Rules |url=https://kotaku.com/hitman-3-year-two-ambrose-island-free-level-agent-47-1849339605 |access-date=2022-08-18 |website=Kotaku |language=en-us |archive-date=10 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220810211728/https://kotaku.com/hitman-3-year-two-ambrose-island-free-level-agent-47-1849339605 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=HITMAN 3 - Ambrose Island (Opening Cinematic) |date=26 July 2022 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0LWgJNXIOuw |language=en |access-date=2022-08-18 |archive-date=18 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818120736/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0LWgJNXIOuw |url-status=live }}</ref>
